title: Checkpoint: Object-Oriented Design
intro: Check that you can choose between inheritance and composition, use ABCs, dataclasses, and enums, and read type hints correctly.

questions.question: Which hint says that scores is a list of integers or None?
questions.explanation: On modern Python, list[int] is the built-in generic and X | None means 'X or None'. Optional[X] from typing is the older spelling of the same thing.

questions.question: An Order class needs to write log messages using a Logger class. Which design is best?
options: Copy the log method into Order
class Logger(Order): make Logger a child
questions.explanation: An order is not a logger, so it fails the is-a test. An order has a logger, which is composition.

questions.question: What happens on the last line?
questions.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Point:
    x: int
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)

p = Point(1)
p.x = 5
questions.explanation: frozen=True makes the dataclass immutable: assigning to a field raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError. field(default_factory=list) gives each instance its own list.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass(order=True)
class Score:
    points: int
    name: str = field(compare=False)

scores = [Score(90, "Aziza"), Score(75, "Bekzod"), Score(90, "Anvar")]
print(max(scores).name, Score(90, "X") == Score(90, "Y"))
questions.explanation: With compare=False, only points is compared. Two scores tie at 90, and max() returns the first one it finds.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
from enum import Enum

class Status(Enum):
    PAID = "paid"

status = Status("paid")
print(status == "paid", status is Status.PAID)
questions.explanation: A plain Enum member is never equal to its raw value. Status("paid") looks up the member, so the is check is True.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
from enum import Enum

class Size(Enum):
    SMALL = "S"
    LARGE = "L"

print(Size["SMALL"].value, Size("L").name)
questions.explanation: Square brackets look up by name and parentheses by value. .value gives "S" and .name gives "LARGE".

questions.question: The hint says list[int], but a tuple is passed. What happens?
options: A type checker error stops the program
questions.explanation: Type hints are not checked at runtime, so the tuple works fine. Only a separate type checker would complain.
